sections.heading: 20.2 Biogeochemical Cycles

blocks.text: Energy flows directionally through ecosystems, entering as sunlight (or inorganic molecules for chemoautotrophs) and leaving as heat during the transfers between trophic levels. Rather than flowing through an ecosystem, the matter that makes up living organisms is conserved and recycled. The six most common elements associated with organic molecules—carbon, nitrogen, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulfur—take a variety of chemical forms and may exist for long periods in the atmosphere, on land, in water, or beneath Earth’s surface. Geologic processes, such as weathering, erosion, water drainage, and the subduction of the tectonic plates, all play a role in the cycling of elements on Earth. Because geology and chemistry have major roles in the study of this process, the recycling of inorganic matter between living organisms and their nonliving environment is called a biogeochemical cycle.

Water, which contains hydrogen and oxygen, is essential to all living processes. The hydrosphere is the area of Earth where water movement and storage occurs: as liquid water on the surface (rivers, lakes, oceans) and beneath the surface (groundwater) or ice, (polar ice caps and glaciers), and as water vapor in the atmosphere. Carbon is found in all organic macromolecules and is an important constituent of fossil fuels. Nitrogen is a major component of our nucleic acids and proteins and is critical to human agriculture. Phosphorus, a major component of nucleic acids, is one of the main ingredients (along with nitrogen) in artificial fertilizers used in agriculture, which has environmental impacts on our surface water. Sulfur, critical to the three-dimensional folding of proteins (as in disulfide binding), is released into the atmosphere by the burning of fossil fuels.

The cycling of these elements is interconnected. For example, the movement of water is critical for the leaching of nitrogen and phosphate into rivers, lakes, and oceans. The ocean is also a major reservoir for carbon. Thus, mineral nutrients are cycled, either rapidly or slowly, through the entire biosphere between the biotic and abiotic world and from one living organism to another.

sections.text: Energy moves in one direction through ecosystems. It enters as sunlight. Chemoautotrophs use inorganic molecules. Energy leaves as heat. This happens between trophic levels. Matter does not flow like energy. It is conserved and recycled. Six elements are common in organic molecules. They are carbon, nitrogen, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulfur. These elements take many chemical forms. They can stay in the atmosphere for a long time. They can also be on land or in water. They may be beneath Earth’s surface. Geologic processes help cycle these elements. Weathering and erosion play a role. Water drainage is also important. The subduction of tectonic plates matters too. Geology and chemistry have major roles in this study. The recycling of inorganic matter is called a biogeochemical cycle. This cycle links living things and the nonliving environment. Water contains hydrogen and oxygen. It is essential to all living processes. The hydrosphere is the area of Earth where water moves. It is also where water is stored. Liquid water is on the surface. This includes rivers, lakes, and oceans. Groundwater is beneath the surface. Ice is found in polar ice caps and glaciers. Water vapor is in the atmosphere. Carbon is in all organic macromolecules. It is an important part of fossil fuels. Nitrogen is a major component of nucleic acids and proteins. It is critical to human agriculture. Phosphorus is a major component of nucleic acids. It is a main ingredient in artificial fertilizers. Nitrogen is also in these fertilizers. These fertilizers are used in agriculture. They have environmental impacts on surface water. Sulfur is critical to the three-dimensional folding of proteins. This is seen in disulfide binding. Burning fossil fuels releases sulfur into the atmosphere. The cycling of these elements is interconnected. Water movement is critical for leaching. It moves nitrogen and phosphate into rivers, lakes, and oceans. The ocean is a major reservoir for carbon. Mineral nutrients cycle through the entire biosphere. This can happen rapidly or slowly. They move between the biotic and abiotic world. They also move from one living organism to another.

items.simple_en: Organisms that make food using energy from inorganic chemical molecules.
items.urdu: وہ جاندار جو کیمیکلز سے اپنی خوراک بناتے ہیں chemoautotrophs کہلاتے ہیں۔
items.example: Some bacteria act as chemoautotrophs in deep ocean vents.

items.simple_en: All the water found on, under, and above Earth's surface.
items.urdu: زمین پر موجود تمام پانی کے ذخائر کو hydrosphere کہتے ہیں۔
items.example: The hydrosphere includes oceans, rivers, and even water vapor.

items.simple_en: Things that are not alive, like rocks, air, and water.
items.urdu: بے جان چیزیں جیسے ہوا اور مٹی nonliving کہلاتی ہیں۔
items.example: Rocks and minerals are nonliving parts of our environment.

items.simple_en: Moving or flowing in only one specific direction.
items.urdu: جب کوئی چیز صرف ایک سمت میں چلے تو اسے directionally کہتے ہیں۔
items.example: Energy flows directionally from the sun through the ecosystem.

items.simple_en: The movement of elements through living things and the Earth.
items.urdu: جانداروں اور زمین کے درمیان مادے کی گردش biogeochemical کہلاتی ہے۔
items.example: The carbon cycle is a well-known biogeochemical process.

items.simple_en: Very large molecules that are essential for living organisms.
items.urdu: بہت بڑے مالیکیولز جیسے پروٹین کو macromolecules کہا جاتا ہے۔
items.example: DNA and proteins are important macromolecules in our bodies.

items.simple_en: The non-living parts of an environment, like sunlight and soil.
items.urdu: ماحول کے بے جان حصے جیسے دھوپ اور مٹی abiotic ہیں۔
items.example: Temperature and water are abiotic factors in an ecosystem.

items.simple_en: Relating to the different levels of a food chain.
items.urdu: خوراک کے مختلف درجوں یا لیول کو trophic کہتے ہیں۔
items.example: Energy is lost as it moves between trophic levels.

items.simple_en: A chemical bond that links two sulfur atoms together.
items.urdu: دو سلفر ایٹمز کے درمیان بننے والے جوڑ کو disulfide کہتے ہیں۔
items.example: A disulfide bond helps proteins maintain their 3D shape.

items.simple_en: The living components of an ecosystem, like plants and animals.
items.urdu: ماحول کے تمام جاندار حصے جیسے پودے اور جانور biotic ہیں۔
items.example: Plants and bacteria are biotic parts of the biosphere.
